question: A kitchen supply line burst and flooded the floor — does exclusion E-17 under form HO-0304 ed. 03-24 bar this water damage claim?
note: No — the E-17 row explicitly confirms burst supply line water damage IS covered (NOT excluded). The trap question from the problem statement.

question: Under form HO-0308 ed. 05-24, does exclusion E-31 reach sinkhole and soil subsidence claims, or only earthquake?
note: All forms — earthquake, landslide, mudslide, sinkhole, subsidence. NOTE: E-31 also exists in HO-0307's table with different wording, so the form number matters.

question: Which exclusion code carries the business pursuits liability exclusion in form HO-0309 ed. 05-24?
note: E-19 — business pursuits liability, BI/PD from any business activity, see CLAUSE BP-1.

question: An insured claims emergency temporary repairs after a named storm but has no photographs or invoices — which exclusion code under HO-0305 ed. 03-24 applies?
note: E-20 — temporary repairs not documented: emergency repairs claimed without photographs or invoices.

question: What is the effective date of endorsement HO-0305 ed. 03-24?
note: March 15, 2024. Stated in SECTION IV (golden) and in the preamble header block (alt). Week 3's famous Q2 miss — a pure form-number lookup.

question: What is the Named Storm deductible for a dwelling insured at $300,000?
note: $6,000 — 2% of $300,000 beats the $5,000 floor. The worked example is in SECTION III (golden); the NS-2 formula chunk (alt) grounds the same computation.

question: A policyholder discovered water damage and reported it five days after discovery — can the claim be denied for late reporting, and under what code?
note: Yes — HO-0304 SECTION III requires reporting within 72 hours of discovery; a late report may be reclassified as gradual seepage and denied under E-11.

question: Is mold remediation ever payable after a covered burst-pipe water loss, and up to what dollar limit?
note: Yes — up to $10,000 under the MF-2 exception, if reported within 72 hours and a licensed contractor provides a written estimate.

question: An earthquake ruptured a gas line and the dwelling caught fire — is the ensuing fire damage excluded as earth movement?
note: No — CLAUSE EM-3 (golden): ensuing fire damage is not excluded. The SECTION III note (alt) restates fire as the only exception.

question: One earring from a scheduled pair was lost — how is the settlement amount calculated?
note: CLAUSE SP-3 — pay the difference between the appraised value of the pair/set and the fair market value of the undamaged item.

question: How recent must an appraisal be for a scheduled item to keep its appraised-value coverage?
note: Dated within 36 months — otherwise the item falls back to the Coverage C sublimits (SECTION III, appraisal requirement).

question: The insured runs a paid after-school care operation at the dwelling and a child was injured — does liability coverage apply?
note: No — CLAUSE BP-3 (golden) excludes home day care, foster care, and after-school care operations regardless of compensation; the E-36 table row (alt) grounds the same denial.
